newsitem.title: RUSSIA: I'll be back at work soon, Yeltsin tells premier.
newsitem.headline: I'll be back at work soon, Yeltsin tells premier.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, recovering from open heart surgery, met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Wednesday and promised to be back soon at his Kremlin desk.
A Kremlin statement said the two men met for 15 minutes in the Cardiology Research Centre where Yeltsin underwent a seven-hour quintuple heart bypass operation on Tuesday.

The statement said that Chernomyrdin, who deputised for Yeltsin for 23 hours, briefed the president on the state of the nation and passed on best wishes for a speedy recovery from many world leaders and ordinary Russians.
"The president heartily thanked all those who supported him before and during the operation and expressed determination to return soon to a full-scale working rhythm," the statement said.
Yeltsin said on September 5 he had agreed to the operation to be able to return to a fully active life.
The meeting with Chernomyrdin was Yeltsin's first official meeting for more than a week.
Separately, the Kremlin press service said doctors had taken Yeltsin off a lung ventilator on Wednesday morning, an important stage in the post-operation period.
It was another sign that the 65-year-old Russian leader was recovering well.
